memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Zebulun will live by the seashore and become a haven for ships; his border will extend toward Sidon.'" — Gen 49:13 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
A short word, and a very ordinary one. Zebulun gets coastline and harbours. Traders, ships, the noise of a working port.

There is no great drama here, no lion imagery, no sceptre. Just a description of where this tribe will live and what they will do. Most lives are like that.

But keep reading Scripture and you find something remarkable. The territory of Zebulun and Naphtali is precisely where Isaiah said a great light would dawn on people walking in darkness — and Matthew tells us Jesus went and lived in that very region, so that the prophecy would be fulfilled (Isa 9:1-2; Matt 4:13-16).

Nazareth was in Zebulun's territory. The Son of God grew up there.

Jacob had no idea. He was simply describing a coastline. But the ordinary patch of ground given to an unremarkable son became the place where the Light of the world would live and work for thirty years.

Do not despise the ordinary place God has put you. Harbours, workplaces, neighbourhoods, homes — these are exactly the sort of places God chooses to show up in.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you view your ordinary circumstances as insignificant?
2. Where might God be at work in a place you have overlooked?
3. How could Christ's light show through you in your everyday setting?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You work in ordinary places. Help me see my daily life as somewhere You are present, and let Your light show through me there. Amen.
